findings.evidence: "The most recent version supersedes the one that came before it."
findings.fix: Either remove this sentence from the reimbursement-log paragraph or clarify what "version" refers to (e.g., "the most recent reimbursement log entry supersedes prior entries for the same claim").
findings.violation: This sentence is attached to the "reimbursement log" review statement, but logs being reviewed monthly don't have "versions" that supersede one another the way a published catalog might; the referent of "version" is unclear here.

findings.evidence: "The stipend clock resumes on their first day back."
findings.fix: Name the specific clock explicitly, e.g., "The 90-day service requirement resumes counting on their first day back."
findings.violation: "Stipend clock" is never defined anywhere else in the document (is it the 90-day service requirement, the benefit-year cutoff, or something else?), making this instruction ambiguous.

findings.evidence: "the stipend request, once the manager signs it, after finance confirms the budget line, moves to final processing"
findings.fix: Rewrite as a simple ordered list, e.g., "First the manager signs the request, then finance confirms the budget line, and the request then moves to final processing."
findings.violation: The nested clause ordering ("once...after...") makes it impossible to tell whether manager sign-off or finance confirmation happens first, or whether both must occur before "final processing."

findings.evidence: "Then, the employee reviews the confirmation summary before submitting the final request."
findings.fix: Clarify whether there are two distinct confirmations (a pre-submission summary and a post-processing email) or correct the sequence so it doesn't conflict.
findings.violation: This contradicts the prior paragraph, which states the employee receives a confirmation email only after processing finishes (i.e., after submission is already complete) - but here the confirmation summary review happens before submission.

findings.evidence: "An incomplete request pauses the timeline until the missing item arrives. The requester gets an automatic reminder after three days."
findings.fix: Specify what "missing item" refers to and standardize on "business days" throughout.
findings.violation: "The missing item" has no antecedent (nothing earlier defines what could be missing from a request), and "after three days" uses a different time unit than the "two business days" used elsewhere in this section, leaving the timeline inconsistent.

findings.evidence: "A photo of the receipt is enough for most requests."
findings.fix: State explicitly which request types or dollar thresholds require additional documentation beyond a photo.
findings.violation: "Most requests" is left vague with no indication of which requests require more than a photo, leaving employees unable to determine their own documentation requirements.

findings.evidence: "You must keep your equipment in good working condition and we may ask for a brief photo check once a year."
findings.fix: Rewrite in third person, e.g., "Employees must keep equipment in good working condition, and the benefits team may request a brief photo check once a year."
findings.violation: This sentence switches to second-person ("You"/"we") voice, inconsistent with the third-person voice ("Employees," "The manager") used throughout the rest of the document.

findings.evidence: "Similarly, the policy applies to one device per category per employee."
findings.fix: Replace "Similarly" with a neutral transition such as "Additionally" or make it its own paragraph.
findings.violation: "Similarly" implies this statement is analogous to the preceding photo-check sentence, but a per-device-category limit is an unrelated rule, not a similar one.

findings.evidence: "Finance reconciles the reimbursable item against the request log each month."
findings.fix: Pick a single term (e.g., "stipend item") and use it consistently across this paragraph.
findings.violation: The paragraph uses three different terms - "stipend item," "reimbursable item," and "covered purchase amount" - for what appears to be the same underlying concept, creating ambiguity about whether these are distinct things or just inconsistent labeling.

findings.evidence: "Also, you submit the request in the portal. Countersign the employee request within two business days. You track its status there until the payment clears."
findings.fix: Add an explicit subject, e.g., "The manager countersigns the employee request within two business days."
findings.violation: The middle sentence drops into imperative mood with no stated subject, breaking continuity with the surrounding "you" (employee) sentences and leaving it unclear who is supposed to countersign.

findings.evidence: "Completing the request begins with confirming eligibility, and the uploaded receipt."
findings.fix: Rewrite as a complete list, e.g., "Completing the request begins with confirming eligibility and uploading the receipt."
findings.violation: The sentence is grammatically malformed - "and the uploaded receipt" is a fragment that doesn't form a coherent second step.

findings.evidence: "The IT asset group updates the equipment catalog after every open enrollment period."
findings.fix: Reconcile which team owns the catalog and on what single schedule it is updated.
findings.violation: This directly contradicts the Program Overview, which states "The benefits team publishes the equipment catalog on the first business day of the month" - the document gives two different owners and two different schedules for the same catalog.

findings.evidence: "A separate audit last spring reviewed unrelated travel expenses. Federal guidance on remote work continues to evolve each year. The office coffee budget was reset at the start of the quarter."
findings.fix: Remove these sentences or move any relevant content to a more appropriate document.
findings.violation: These three sentences are unrelated to the home-office equipment stipend policy and don't belong in a section about program coordination responsibility.

findings.evidence: "The finance office also flags any request that repeats within the same quarter."
findings.fix: Clarify whether repeat requests are possible under the one-claim-per-year rule, or remove this flagging rule if it's inapplicable.
findings.violation: This contradicts the Eligibility section's rule that the stipend "covers one claim per employee per benefit year" - if only one claim per year is permitted, a repeat claim within the same quarter should already be disallowed, not merely "flagged."

findings.evidence: "The most recent version supersedes the one that came before it."
findings.fix: Write a version of this sentence specific to the vendor list, or remove it if redundant.
findings.violation: This sentence is reused verbatim from the Program Overview section (originally describing the reimbursement log), now applied to the vendor list, suggesting careless copy-paste rather than a deliberate, verified statement about vendor-list versioning.
